subproblem.title: Mass densities are unique
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), x ∈ ℝ^P (= Euclid P) and θ, θ' ∈ ℝ. Suppose HasMassDensity T x θ and HasMassDensity T x θ', i.e. θ ≥ 0, θ' ≥ 0, and the ratio T.massOn(B_ρ(x)) / (ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) ∈ [0, ∞] (ω_n = unitBallVolume n, B_ρ(x) the open ball) tends both to ofReal θ and to ofReal θ' as ρ → 0⁺ (filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ). Then θ = θ'.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (x : Euclid P) (θ θ' : ℝ), HasMassDensity T x θ → HasMassDensity T x θ' → θ = θ'
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof ("Densities are unique: if HasMassDensity S x θ and HasMassDensity S x θ', the two limits along the nontrivial filter 𝓝[>] 0 in the Hausdorff space ℝ≥0∞ agree, so ofReal θ = ofReal θ', and θ, θ' ≥ 0 give θ = θ'"), stated for an arbitrary domain U and current T. Simon defines Θ^n(μ_T, x) as a limit (Ch. 7, 7.3.1; contract definition HasMassDensity), so it is unique when it exists.
Notation: f(ρ) := T.massOn(B_ρ(x)) / (unitBallVolume n · ENNReal.ofReal(ρ^n)) ∈ [0, ∞] for ρ ∈ ℝ. By definition, HasMassDensity T x θ means 0 ≤ θ and f(ρ) → ENNReal.ofReal θ as ρ → 0⁺, i.e. along the filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ.
1. The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is nontrivial: each of its members contains an interval (0, ε) with ε > 0, which is nonempty (ℝ is densely ordered without maximum; Mathlib provides the NeBot instance for 𝓝[>] a).
2. [0, ∞] = ℝ≥0∞ with its order topology is a Hausdorff space, and in a Hausdorff space a function has at most one limit along a nontrivial filter (tendsto_nhds_unique). By the two hypotheses, f → ofReal θ and f → ofReal θ' along 𝓝[>] 0. By step 1 the filter is nontrivial, so ofReal θ = ofReal θ'.
3. ENNReal.ofReal is injective on [0, ∞): for p, q ≥ 0, ofReal p = ofReal q iff p = q (ENNReal.ofReal_eq_ofReal_iff). The first components of the hypotheses give θ ≥ 0 and θ' ≥ 0, so step 2 yields θ = θ'. ∎
proof_key_steps: 𝓝[>] 0 is a nontrivial filter on ℝ and ℝ≥0∞ is Hausdorff, so the two density limits coincide: ofReal θ = ofReal θ'.
θ ≥ 0, θ' ≥ 0 and injectivity of ENNReal.ofReal on [0, ∞) give θ = θ'.

audit.reason: The identical density ratios have unique limits along the nontrivial right-neighborhood filter. Nonnegativity permits injectivity of ENNReal.ofReal. The proof covers the exact arbitrary-domain statement without additional hypotheses.

subproblem.title: Translation invariance of f·Hⁿ for a translation-invariant density f
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P, f : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] an arbitrary function (no measurability assumed), and y ∈ ℝ^P with f(y + x) = f(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Let ν := H^n.withDensity f, so ν(B) = ∫⁻_B f dH^n for Borel B. Then ν((x ↦ y + x)⁻¹(A)) = ν(A) for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P; that is, ν(A − y) = ν(A).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞) (y : Euclid P), (∀ x : Euclid P, f (y + x) = f x) → ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).withDensity f ((fun x => y + x) ⁻¹' A) = (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).withDensity f A
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof (translation invariance (i)), with the density function ofReal ∘ Θ of the parent replaced by an arbitrary f : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] satisfying f(y + ·) = f. The parent's computation μ(A − y) = ∫_{A−y} ofReal Θ dH^n = ∫_A ofReal Θ(x − y) dH^n(x) = ∫_A ofReal Θ dH^n is the same change of variables, written here through the preimage form.
Notation: τ(x) := y + x on ℝ^P, H^n = μHE[n], and ν := H^n.withDensity f.
1. τ is a bijective isometry of ℝ^P (|τ(a) − τ(b)| = |a − b|, inverse x ↦ −y + x); in Mathlib it is IsometryEquiv.addLeft y. In particular τ is a homeomorphism, hence a measurable embedding for the Borel σ-algebra (Homeomorph.addLeft y). Since τ is continuous, τ⁻¹(A) is Borel whenever A is.
2. H^n is invariant under bijective isometries: τ_#H^n = H^n, i.e. τ is measure preserving from (ℝ^P, H^n) to (ℝ^P, H^n) (IsometryEquiv.measurePreserving_euclideanHausdorffMeasure). The reason is that μHE[n] is a constant multiple of the Hausdorff measure μH[n], which is defined through diameters only.
3. Change of variables. For a measure-preserving measurable embedding τ, every function g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] and every set B ⊆ ℝ^P, ∫⁻_{τ⁻¹(B)} g(τ(a)) dH^n(a) = ∫⁻_B g dH^n (MeasurePreserving.setLIntegral_comp_preimage_emb; no measurability of g is needed because τ is a measurable embedding). With g := f and B := A this reads ∫⁻_{τ⁻¹(A)} f(y + a) dH^n(a) = ∫⁻_A f dH^n.
4. By hypothesis f(y + a) = f(a) for every a ∈ ℝ^P, so the left side of step 3 equals ∫⁻_{τ⁻¹(A)} f dH^n.
5. For Borel B, ν(B) = ∫⁻_B f dH^n (withDensity_apply; only measurability of B is needed). Both A and τ⁻¹(A) are Borel by step 1. So ν(τ⁻¹(A)) = ∫⁻_{τ⁻¹(A)} f dH^n = ∫⁻_A f dH^n = ν(A), using steps 3 and 4. ∎
proof_key_steps: x ↦ y + x is a bijective isometry, hence a measurable embedding that preserves μHE[n].
Change of variables for lower integrals along a measure-preserving embedding, together with f(y + ·) = f, gives ∫⁻_{(y+·)⁻¹A} f dH^n = ∫⁻_A f dH^n, i.e. ν((y+·)⁻¹A) = ν(A).

audit.reason: Translation is a measure-preserving measurable embedding for μHE[n]. The cited preimage change-of-variables formula applies to arbitrary f, and its orientation matches the stated preimage conclusion.

subproblem.title: The density equals the multiplicity Hⁿ-a.e. on the carrier
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation of S in ℝ^P (R : IMRep univ n with R.Represents S; M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult). Let Θ : ℝ^P → ℝ satisfy HasMassDensity S x Θ(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Then Θ(x) = θ(x) (θ(x) ∈ ℕ cast to ℝ) for H^n⌞M-a.e. x, i.e. for almost every x with respect to μHE[n] restricted to R.carrier.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (Θ : Euclid P → ℝ), R.Represents S → (∀ x : Euclid P, HasMassDensity S x (Θ x)) → ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict R.carrier), Θ x = (R.mult x : ℝ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof ("Θ = θ for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M"), together with the remark in step 2 that μ and ν := H^n⌞M have the same null sets inside M. In Simon this is Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2) with Theorem 1.9 (chapter-03.txt lines 298–325), as used in Ch. 4, 3.12 (chapter-04.txt lines 350–354: "Θ^n(V, x) = θ(x) for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M (by Remark 1.8(2))"). (The parent's citation "Ch. 4, Remark 1.8(2)" refers to this remark of Ch. 3.) The pointwise statement of step 3 — approximate tangent planes (α), Besicovitch–Lebesgue points (β) and the computation 3(a)–(b) — is exactly the sibling ae_density_mult (the reused accepted declaration Submission.rsd_ae_hasMassDensity_mult), whose accepted proof carries out that argument. It is used here as a black box.
Notation: M = R.carrier (a Borel set), θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ, H^n = μHE[n], ν := H^n⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M, and μ := R.measure = ν.withDensity θ, so μ(B) = ∫⁻_B θ dν for Borel B.
1. Apply the sibling ae_density_mult with U := ℝ^P (open), T := S and R; R.Represents S is a hypothesis. It gives HasMassDensity S x θ(x) for μ-a.e. x, with θ(x) cast to ℝ.
2. Let x be such a point. By hypothesis also HasMassDensity S x Θ(x), so the sibling density_unique (U := ℝ^P, T := S) gives Θ(x) = θ(x). Hence Θ(x) = θ(x) for μ-a.e. x, i.e. the set Z := {x : Θ(x) ≠ θ(x)} satisfies μ(Z) = 0 (μ applied to an arbitrary set is its outer measure).
3. ν ≪ μ.
- The function x ↦ θ(x) ∈ [0, ∞] is Borel: θ : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable (axiom measurable_mult), and every map out of ℕ (discrete σ-algebra) is measurable, in particular the cast ℕ → [0, ∞].
- θ(x) ≥ 1 for every x ∈ M (axiom mult_pos). Since ν is carried by the Borel set M, θ(x) ≠ 0 for ν-a.e. x.
- Let B be Borel with μ(B) = 0. Then ∫⁻_B θ dν = 0, so θ = 0 ν-a.e. on B; as θ ≠ 0 ν-a.e., ν(B) = 0. (This is Mathlib's withDensity_absolutelyContinuous': ν ≪ ν.withDensity θ when θ is ν-a.e. measurable and ν-a.e. nonzero.)
- For an arbitrary set Z with μ(Z) = 0 choose a Borel set B ⊇ Z with μ(B) = 0 (measurable superset of a null set). Then ν(Z) ≤ ν(B) = 0.
4. By steps 2 and 3, ν(Z) = 0. That is, Θ(x) = θ(x) for ν-a.e. x, where ν = μHE[n].restrict R.carrier. This is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: The reused accepted density theorem (sibling ae_density_mult) gives HasMassDensity S x θ(x) for μ_R-a.e. x.
Uniqueness of densities (sibling density_unique) turns this into Θ = θ μ_R-a.e.
Since θ ≥ 1 on M, H^n⌞M ≪ μ_R = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ, so Θ = θ holds H^n⌞M-a.e.

audit.reason: The accepted density theorem and uniqueness give equality R.measure-a.e. Measurability and positivity of multiplicity establish the required absolute continuity in the correct direction, transferring equality to Hausdorff measure restricted to the carrier.

subproblem.title: n-homogeneity of f·Hⁿ for a dilation-invariant density f
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P, f : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] an arbitrary function (no measurability assumed), and λ > 0 with f(λx) = f(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Let ν := H^n.withDensity f. Then for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P, ν(λA) = λ^n·ν(A), where λA = (x ↦ λx)(A) is the image of A; in [0, ∞] this reads ν(λA) = ofReal(λ^n)·ν(A).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞) (lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → (∀ x : Euclid P, f (lam • x) = f x) → ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).withDensity f ((fun x => lam • x) '' A) = ENNReal.ofReal (lam ^ n) * (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).withDensity f A
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof (homogeneity (ii)), with the density function ofReal ∘ Θ replaced by an arbitrary f satisfying f(λ·) = f. The change of variables ∫_{λA} g dH^n = λ^n ∫_A g(λw) dH^n(w) used there is the sibling dilation_change_of_variables (the reused accepted declaration Submission.euclid_hausdorff_dilation_change_of_variables, which step 7 cites).
Notation: δ(x) := λx on ℝ^P, H^n = μHE[n], ν := H^n.withDensity f, and D := δ(A) = λA.
1. δ is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse x ↦ λ⁻¹x (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero λ, λ ≠ 0). Hence δ is a measurable embedding and injective. So D = δ(A) is Borel (the image of a Borel set under a measurable embedding), and δ⁻¹(D) = A by injectivity.
2. Apply part (ii) of the sibling dilation_change_of_variables with c := λ > 0, M := D and g := f. It gives ∫⁻_{δ⁻¹(D)} f(λz) dH^n(z) = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n) · ∫⁻_D f dH^n; it holds for every f : ℝ^P → [0, ∞].
3. By step 1, δ⁻¹(D) = A, and by hypothesis f(λz) = f(z) for every z. So step 2 becomes ∫⁻_A f dH^n = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n) · ∫⁻_D f dH^n.
4. A and D are Borel, so ν(A) = ∫⁻_A f dH^n and ν(D) = ∫⁻_D f dH^n (withDensity_apply). Hence ν(A) = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n) · ν(D).
5. Multiply both sides by ofReal(λ^n). Since λ^n ≥ 0 and λ⁻¹^n ≥ 0, ofReal(λ^n) · ofReal(λ⁻¹^n) = ofReal(λ^n · λ⁻¹^n) = ofReal((λ · λ⁻¹)^n) = ofReal(1) = 1, using λ ≠ 0. Therefore ofReal(λ^n) · ν(A) = ν(D) = ν(λA). ∎
proof_key_steps: x ↦ λx is a homeomorphism, so λA is Borel and (λ·)⁻¹(λA) = A.
The reused change of variables (sibling dilation_change_of_variables) with g = f and f(λ·) = f gives ν(A) = λ^{-n} ν(λA).
Multiplying by ofReal(λ^n) gives ν(λA) = ofReal(λ^n)·ν(A).

subproblem.title: The density vanishes Hⁿ-a.e. off the carrier (Upper Density Theorem)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation of S in ℝ^P (R : IMRep univ n with R.Represents S; M = R.carrier). Let Θ : ℝ^P → ℝ satisfy HasMassDensity S x Θ(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Then H^n({x ∈ ℝ^P : x ∉ M and Θ(x) > 0}) = 0, where H^n = μHE[n] (evaluated as an outer measure).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (Θ : Euclid P → ℝ), R.Represents S → (∀ x : Euclid P, HasMassDensity S x (Θ x)) → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)) {x | x ∉ R.carrier ∧ 0 < Θ x} = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof ("Θ = 0 for H^n-a.e. x ∉ M"). In Simon this is the Upper Density Theorem, Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2) (chapter-01.txt lines 700–722), which is derived from the comparison Theorem 3.3 (line 602) and the 5-times covering Lemma 3.4. The three ingredients of step 4 are reused accepted declarations:
- the Vitali 5r-covering estimate μH[n]_{10δ}(A) ≤ 10^n (tω_n)^{-1} μ(U') (letting δ ↓ 0) is the sibling lower_density_comparison (Submission.dorag_sn_hausdorff_le_mul_of_lower_density);
- "by outer regularity there is an open U' ⊇ A with μ(U') < ε" is the sibling null_open_superset (Submission.dorag_sn_open_superset_measure_lt);
- the identity S.massOn(B_ρ(x)) = μ(B_ρ(x)) of step 1 (im_mass_measure (a)) is the sibling mass_eq_measure (Submission.rsd_massOn_eq_measure, which states exactly im_mass_measure (a)).
Notation: M = R.carrier (Borel), θ = R.mult, H^n = μHE[n], μ := R.measure = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ, ω_n := unitBallVolume n = Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝ^n. B_ρ(x) is the open ball and B̄_ρ(x) the closed ball.
1. Constants. 0 < ω_n < ∞: the open unit ball of ℝ^n is nonempty, open and bounded, and Lebesgue measure is positive on nonempty open sets and finite on bounded sets. This includes n = 0, where ℝ^0 is a point and ω_0 = 1.
2. Mass equals measure on balls. For every x ∈ ℝ^P and ρ ∈ ℝ, B_ρ(x) is an open subset of ℝ^P. So the sibling mass_eq_measure with U := ℝ^P (open), T := S and W := B_ρ(x) gives S.massOn(B_ρ(x)) = μ(B_ρ(x)).
3. μ vanishes off M. Since M is Borel, μ(ℝ^P ∖ M) = ∫⁻_{ℝ^P∖M} θ d(H^n⌞M) = ∫⁻ θ d(H^n⌞((ℝ^P ∖ M) ∩ M)) = 0, because (ℝ^P ∖ M) ∩ M = ∅.
4. μ is locally finite. Let x ∈ ℝ^P. The closed ball B̄_1(x) is compact (ℝ^P is proper) and contained in ℝ^P = U. So μ(B_1(x)) ≤ μ(B̄_1(x)) = ∫⁻_{M∩B̄_1(x)} θ dH^n < ∞ by the axiom locallyIntegrable_mult.
5. Fix k ∈ ℕ and put t := 1/(k+1) > 0 and A := {x ∉ M : Θ(x) > t}. By step 3 and monotonicity, μ(A) ≤ μ(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0.
6. Lower density bound on A. Put c := t·ω_n, a positive real number by step 1. Let x ∈ A and write f(s) := S.massOn(B_s(x)) / (ω_n · ofReal(s^n)).
- Since HasMassDensity S x Θ(x), f(s) → ofReal Θ(x) as s → 0⁺. As 0 ≤ t < Θ(x), ofReal t < ofReal Θ(x), so (ofReal t, ∞] is a neighbourhood of the limit. Hence there is t₀ > 0 with f(s) > ofReal t for every s ∈ (0, t₀).
- Fix s ∈ (0, t₀). The denominator d := ω_n · ofReal(s^n) satisfies 0 < d < ∞ (step 1 and s^n > 0). So ofReal t < S.massOn(B_s(x))/d gives ofReal t · d ≤ S.massOn(B_s(x)) (ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le).
- Since t, ω_n and s^n are nonnegative and ω_n < ∞, ofReal t · d = ofReal(t · ω_n · s^n) = ofReal(c s^n).
- With step 2 and B_s(x) ⊆ B̄_s(x): ofReal(c s^n) ≤ S.massOn(B_s(x)) = μ(B_s(x)) ≤ μ(B̄_s(x)) for all s ∈ (0, t₀).
7. Comparison. The sibling lower_density_comparison with N := P, this n, and c > 0 gives a constant C ∈ [0, ∞) (C ≠ ∞) such that, for the measure ν := μ, every open O ⊇ A satisfies H^n(A) ≤ C · μ(O); its density hypothesis is step 6.
8. Small open neighbourhoods. Let ε ∈ (0, ∞]. By step 5, μ(A) = 0, and by step 4 every x ∈ A has a radius r = 1 with μ(B_r(x)) < ∞. So the sibling null_open_superset gives an open O ⊇ A with μ(O) < ε. By step 7, H^n(A) ≤ C · μ(O) ≤ C · ε.
9. Take ε := 1/j for j ∈ ℕ (in [0, ∞], 1/0 = ∞ > 0 and 1/j > 0 for every j). Since C < ∞, C · (1/j) → C · 0 = 0 as j → ∞ (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul with ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero). Passing to the limit in H^n(A) ≤ C · (1/j) gives H^n(A) ≤ 0, hence H^n(A) = 0.
10. Union over t. If x ∉ M and Θ(x) > 0, the Archimedean property gives k ∈ ℕ with 1/(k+1) < Θ(x). So {x ∉ M : Θ(x) > 0} ⊆ ⋃_{k∈ℕ} {x ∉ M : Θ(x) > 1/(k+1)}. By step 9 each set in the union is H^n-null, and countable subadditivity together with monotonicity gives H^n({x ∉ M : Θ(x) > 0}) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: μ_R vanishes off M, is locally finite, and S.massOn = μ_R on open balls (sibling mass_eq_measure).
On A_t = {x ∉ M : Θ(x) > t} the density hypothesis gives μ_R(B̄_s(x)) ≥ t ω_n s^n for small s.

Vitali comparison (sibling lower_density_comparison) gives H^n(A_t) ≤ C μ_R(O) for every open O ⊇ A_t, and outer regularity at the μ_R-null set A_t (sibling null_open_superset) makes μ_R(O) arbitrarily small, so H^n(A_t) = 0.
A countable union over t = 1/(k+1) gives H^n({x ∉ M : Θ(x) > 0}) = 0.

audit.reason: Carrier concentration, compact local finiteness and mass equality on balls justify the setup. Positive finite denominators yield the lower-density bound; comparison and arbitrarily small open neighborhoods make each threshold set Hausdorff-null. The countable union handles arbitrary, potentially nonmeasurable threshold sets correctly.

subproblem.title: μ_R = Θ·Hⁿ when the density exists everywhere
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation of S in ℝ^P (R : IMRep univ n with R.Represents S). Let Θ : ℝ^P → ℝ satisfy HasMassDensity S x Θ(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Then R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M is equal to H^n.withDensity(x ↦ ofReal Θ(x)), where H^n = μHE[n]; equivalently μ_R(A) = ∫⁻_A ofReal Θ dH^n for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (Θ : Euclid P → ℝ), R.Represents S → (∀ x : Euclid P, HasMassDensity S x (Θ x)) → R.measure = (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (Θ x))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof ("By steps 3 and 4 and Θ ≥ 0, ofReal ∘ Θ = θ·1_M H^n-a.e. Therefore for every Borel A, ∫_A ofReal Θ dH^n = ∫_{A∩M} θ dH^n = μ(A)"). In Simon this is the canonical representative V = v(M_V, θ_V) with θ_V(x) = Θ^n(V, x) of Ch. 4, 3.12 (chapter-04.txt lines 350–354). Here it holds without stationarity because Θ is assumed to exist at every point.
Notation: M = R.carrier (Borel), θ = R.mult, H^n = μHE[n], μ := R.measure = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ, and f(x) := ofReal Θ(x) ∈ [0, ∞]. No measurability of f is assumed or needed: lower integrals ∫⁻ are defined for every function, and a.e.-equal functions have equal lower integrals.
1. Reduction. Two measures on ℝ^P are equal as soon as they agree on all Borel sets (Measure.ext). Fix a Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P.
2. Left side. μ(A) = ∫⁻_A θ d(H^n⌞M) = ∫⁻_{A∩M} θ dH^n. This uses withDensity_apply for the Borel set A and (H^n⌞M)⌞A = H^n⌞(A ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict).
3. Right side. (H^n.withDensity f)(A) = ∫⁻_A f dH^n (withDensity_apply). Splitting A along the Borel set M, ∫⁻_A f dH^n = ∫⁻_{A∩M} f dH^n + ∫⁻_{A∖M} f dH^n (lintegral_inter_add_sdiff; this is additivity of the restricted measure H^n⌞A = H^n⌞(A∩M) + H^n⌞(A∖M) and holds for every f).
4. The part A ∩ M. By the sibling density_eq_mult, Θ(x) = θ(x) for H^n⌞M-a.e. x. Since A ∩ M ⊆ M, the same holds for H^n⌞(A∩M)-a.e. x (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset). At such x, f(x) = ofReal θ(x) = θ(x), because ofReal of a natural number is that number in [0, ∞]. Hence ∫⁻_{A∩M} f dH^n = ∫⁻_{A∩M} θ dH^n (lintegral_congr_ae).
5. The part A ∖ M.
- Let N := {x : x ∉ M and Θ(x) > 0}; by the sibling null_off_carrier, H^n(N) = 0.
- Let x ∈ A ∖ M with f(x) ≠ 0. Then f(x) > 0, and ofReal p > 0 iff p > 0, so Θ(x) > 0 and x ∈ N. Thus {x : x ∈ A ∖ M and f(x) ≠ 0} ⊆ N is H^n-null; that is, H^n-a.e. x satisfies (x ∈ A ∖ M ⇒ f(x) = 0).
- As A ∖ M is Borel, this means f = 0 for H^n⌞(A∖M)-a.e. x (ae_restrict_iff'). Hence ∫⁻_{A∖M} f dH^n = ∫⁻_{A∖M} 0 dH^n = 0.
6. Conclusion. By steps 3, 4, 5 and 2, (H^n.withDensity f)(A) = ∫⁻_{A∩M} θ dH^n + 0 = μ(A). As A was an arbitrary Borel set, step 1 gives R.measure = μHE[n].withDensity (x ↦ ofReal Θ(x)). ∎
proof_key_steps: Compare both measures on a Borel set A and split ∫⁻_A ofReal Θ dH^n along the carrier M.
On A ∩ M, ofReal Θ = θ H^n-a.e. (sibling density_eq_mult), giving ∫⁻_{A∩M} θ dH^n = μ_R(A).
On A ∖ M, ofReal Θ = 0 H^n-a.e. (sibling null_off_carrier), so that part vanishes.

audit.reason: Comparison on Borel sets and splitting along the measurable carrier prove measure equality using exactly the two declared dependencies. Lower-integral congruence and the off-carrier null-set argument require no additional measurability of Θ.
